channel.title: My DSA Journey — Weekly Digest
channel.description: Weekly rotation of one real-world case study, one pattern drill, and one hard-mode challenge from the 30-week DSA Journey.

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W41
item.description: Case study: How "Discover Weekly" is a Graph + Matrix Factorization Problem Pattern drill (Week 22, #2): Given a directed graph that may contain negative edge weights (no negative cycles), find shortest distances from `s`. n ≤ 500. Challenge 2 (Week 22): Negative-Weight Cycle Detection (Bellman–Ford)

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W40
item.description: Case study: How Google Maps Uses Dijkstra (and Why They Also Use Bidirectional A*) Pattern drill (Week 21, #1): Given an array of n ≤ 10^5 integers and up to 10^5 queries each asking the sum of `a[l..r]`, with point updates `a[i] = v` interspersed, answer each operation in O(log n). Challenge 1 (Week 21): Segment Tree With Lazy Propagation (Range Add, Range Sum)

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W39
item.description: Case study: real\_world Pattern drill (Week 20, #10): Distractor: Given n ≤ 1000 items with weights and a knapsack capacity, find the maximum value subset. (Backtracking?) Challenge 5 (Week 20): Generate All Valid Parentheses Combinations

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W38
item.description: Case study: Graph Coloring in Compilers Pattern drill (Week 19, #9): Distractor: Given arbitrary coin denominations and a target sum, find the minimum number of coins. (Same as 8?) Challenge 3 (Week 19): Huffman Coding Build + Encode + Decode

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W37
item.description: Case study: PageRank as a Graph Algorithm Pattern drill (Week 18, #8): Given a string of length n ≤ 500, find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence (not necessarily contiguous). Challenge 2 (Week 18): Longest Increasing Subsequence in O(n log n)

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W36
item.description: Case study: What grep / ripgrep Actually Do Pattern drill (Week 17, #7): Distractor: Given a weighted graph with non-negative edges, find the shortest path from `s` to `t`. (Is BFS enough?) Challenge 2 (Week 17): Count Distinct Shortest Paths in an Unweighted Graph

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W35
item.description: Case study: Rope Data Structure in VS Code / Sublime Pattern drill (Week 16, #6): Distractor: Given a *sorted* array and a target sum, find a pair summing to T. (Should you use a hash set?) Challenge 1 (Week 16): Custom Open-Addressing HashMap

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W34
item.description: Case study: B-trees vs LSM Trees vs Hash Indexes Pattern drill (Week 15, #5): Given an array of CPU tasks with cooldown constraints (same task needs ≥ n idle time between consecutive runs), return the minimum total time. Up to 10^4 tasks. Challenge 3 (Week 15): K-th Largest Element With Constant-Memory Online Selection

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W33
item.description: Case study: Bloom Filters for Safe Browsing Pattern drill (Week 14, #4): Given two nodes `u` and `v` in a binary tree, find their lowest common ancestor. n ≤ 10^5. Challenge 2 (Week 14): Lowest Common Ancestor in a BST and in a General Binary Tree

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W32
item.description: Case study: Token Bucket vs Sliding Window at Cloudflare/AWS Pattern drill (Week 13, #3): Given an undirected graph with up to 10^5 nodes, find the shortest path (in edges) from node `s` to every other node. Challenge 1 (Week 13): Sliding Window Maximum via Monotonic Deque

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W31
item.description: Case study: LRU vs LFU vs ARC in Redis Pattern drill (Week 12, #2): Evaluate a postfix arithmetic expression with tokens `+ - * /` and integer operands. Length up to 10^5. Challenge 4 (Week 12): Next Greater Element — Circular Array Variant

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W30
item.description: Case study: How Ranking Interacts with Sorting + Priority Queues Pattern drill (Week 11, #1): Given the head of a singly linked list of up to 10^5 nodes, detect whether it contains a cycle. O(1) extra space. Challenge 3 (Week 11): LRU Cache From Scratch (No Library Containers)

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W29
item.description: Case study: Git's Commit Graph as a DAG, Why Topological Sort Matters Pattern drill (Week 10, #10): Given an `n × n` matrix, find the saddle point if any (minimum in its row AND maximum in its column). Challenge 2 (Week 10): Set Matrix Zeroes With O(1) Extra Space

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W28
item.description: Case study: Token Bucket vs Sliding Window at Cloudflare/AWS Pattern drill (Week 9, #9): Sort an array containing only 0/1 values in place, single pass, O(1) extra space. Challenge 1 (Week 9): Count Inversions Using Merge Sort

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W27
item.description: Case study: LRU vs LFU vs ARC in Redis Pattern drill (Week 8, #8): Find the integer square root of n (largest `k` with `k*k ≤ n`), n up to 10^18. Challenge 4 (Week 8): Aggressive Cows / Maximum Minimum Distance

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W26
item.description: Case study: How Ranking Interacts with Sorting + Priority Queues Pattern drill (Week 7, #7): Distractor: Given two strings `s` and `t` of length up to 10^6, decide whether `t` occurs in `s`. (Naïve is too slow — what now?) Challenge 3 (Week 7): KMP With Multiple Patterns at Once

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W25
item.description: Case study: Git's Commit Graph as a DAG, Why Topological Sort Matters Pattern drill (Week 6, #6): Given an array, move all zeros to the end, preserving the relative order of non-zero elements. In place. Challenge 2 (Week 6): In-Place Multi-Block Rotation

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W24
item.description: Case study: How Priority Queues Power a Real-Time Feed Pattern drill (Week 5, #5): Compute `gcd(a, b)` for positive integers a, b ≤ 10^9. Challenge 2 (Week 5): Mutual Recursion: Hofstadter Female/Male

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W23
item.description: Case study: Caching Strategies in DNS Resolvers Pattern drill (Week 4, #4): Print Pascal's triangle up to row `n` (n ≤ 20), each row centered. Challenge 1 (Week 4): Hollow Diamond With Border

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W22
item.description: Case study: Why Your CDN Uses Consistent Hashing (and What Happens Without It) Pattern drill (Week 3, #3): Given an integer `n`, determine whether it is a power of two. n fits in 32 bits. Challenge 3 (Week 3): Generalized Fibonacci (Pisano Period)

item.title: Weekly Digest 2026-W21
item.description: Case study: How "Discover Weekly" is a Graph + Matrix Factorization Problem Pattern drill (Week 2, #2): Read an integer score 0–100 and print the letter grade: A (>=90), B (>=80), C (>=70), D (>=60), F otherwise. Challenge 2 (Week 2): Tax Bracket Salary Computer
